11-1.bio:
Saints Kosmas and Damian of Asia Minor were brothers and physicians, raised in the faith by their pious mother Theodota. They treated the sick without ever accepting payment, asking only that those they healed believe in Christ, and for this the Church calls them Unmercenaries. They reposed in peace after lives given wholly to God and neighbor.

They are the first of several pairs of unmercenary physicians named Kosmas and Damian honored in the church year, and they are invoked by the sick and by those in the healing professions. They are commemorated on November 1.
11-1.desc: Holy Unmercenary Physicians Cosmas and Damian of Asia.
11-1.name: Kosmas and Damian (Asian)

11-1.bio:
Venerable David the Elder was a monk of the sixteenth century who, after years of ascetic struggle and travels in Greece and beyond, settled in the mountains of northern Euboea and founded the monastery of the Transfiguration, known today as the monastery of Saint David.

Tradition relates that he was renowned for his humility, his gifts of prayer and his care for the enslaved Greek population under Ottoman rule. His monastery remains a place of pilgrimage, and he is venerated as the patron of Euboea.
11-1.desc: Venerable David the Elder, ascetic and founder of the monastery that bears his name in northern Euboea.
11-1.name: David of Euboea

11-1.bio:
Saint Helen was a young woman of Sinope on the Black Sea coast of Asia Minor. Tradition relates that a local Ottoman official, struck by her beauty, tried to force her to renounce Christ and marry him; she refused steadfastly.

She was imprisoned and tortured, and finally put to death for her faith. Her relics were honoured by the Greek Christians of Sinope and later carried to Greece by refugees, where her veneration continues.
11-1.desc: Virgin Martyr Helen of Sinope, a young Christian who suffered for her faith under Ottoman rule.
11-1.name: Helen of Sinope

11-1.bio:
The holy women Kyriaina and Juliana suffered for Christ in Cilicia during the persecutions of the early fourth century. Tradition relates that they were publicly humiliated and paraded through the city before being burned alive.

They are commemorated together as a witness to the courage of Christian women under the persecutions of Maximian.
11-1.desc: Holy Martyrs Kyriaina and Juliana, who suffered together in Cilicia.
11-1.name: Kyriaina and Juliana

11-1.bio:
The seven holy martyrs Caesarius, Dasius, Sabbas, Sabinianus, Agrippa, Adrian and Thomas suffered for Christ at Damascus. The synaxarion records that they were beheaded after confessing their faith.

Little else is preserved about their lives, but their names have been kept in the Church's calendar as a group of confessors who died together.
11-1.desc: Holy Martyrs Caesarius, Dasius, Sabbas, Sabinianus, Agrippa, Adrian and Thomas, who suffered at Damascus.
11-1.name: Caesarius, Dasius and companions

11-1.bio:
Saint James was born in Kastoria in northern Greece and, after a period as a wealthy merchant, renounced the world and became a monk on Mount Athos. He later lived as an ascetic in Greece with his disciples, the deacon James and the monk Dionysios.

Tradition relates that in the sixteenth century they were denounced to the Ottoman authorities, imprisoned and tortured at Adrianople, and finally hanged for refusing to deny Christ.
11-1.desc: Holy New Monk-Martyr James of Kastoria with his disciples James the Deacon and Dionysios the Monk.
11-1.name: James of Kastoria and his disciples

11-1.bio:
Saint Theodota was the mother of the Holy Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian of Asia. Widowed early, she raised her sons in piety and the fear of God, and tradition credits her upbringing with their later life of healing without payment.

She is commemorated together with her sons on the day of their feast.
11-1.desc: Righteous Theodota, the pious mother of the Holy Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian.
11-1.name: Theodota, mother of Cosmas and Damian

11-10.bio:
The holy apostle Erastos, one of the Seventy, is named by the Apostle Paul in his epistle to the Romans as the treasurer of the city of Corinth. A companion of Paul in the work of the Gospel, he served the growing Church with the same faithfulness he had shown in civic office.

Tradition remembers him as continuing in ministry among the first generation of Christians, laboring for the spread of the faith. He is commemorated on November 10.
11-10.name: Erastos the Apostle

11-10.bio:
The Apostles Olympas, Herodion, Sosipater, Quartus and Tertius are among the Seventy and are greeted by Saint Paul in his Epistle to the Romans. Tradition relates that Herodion became bishop of Neopatras, Sosipater of Iconium, Quartus of Beirut and Tertius of Iconium after Sosipater.

Olympas and Herodion are said to have been beheaded in Rome on the day of the Apostle Peter's martyrdom.
11-10.desc: Holy Apostles of the Seventy Olympas, Herodion, Sosipater, Quartus and Tertius, named in Romans 16.
11-10.name: Olympas, Herodion, Sosipater and Quartus the Apostles

11-10.bio:
Saint Arsenios was born in Farasa of Cappadocia in the nineteenth century and served as priest and teacher of his village for some fifty years, known for his ascetic life and the many healings worked through his prayers. He baptized the infant who would become Saint Paisios the Athonite.

He led his people to Greece in the population exchange of 1924 and reposed in Corfu forty days later, as he had foretold. He was glorified in 1986.
11-10.desc: Venerable Arsenios of Cappadocia, priest of Farasa and spiritual father of Saint Paisios.
11-10.name: Arsenios of Cappadocia

11-10.bio:
Saint Orestes was a physician of Tyana in Cappadocia during the persecution of Diocletian. Arrested for his faith, he refused to sacrifice to the idols and was subjected to severe tortures.

Tradition relates that he was finally tied to a wild horse and dragged to death. His name remains in use as a Greek baptismal name.
11-10.desc: Holy Martyr Orestes of Tyana in Cappadocia, a physician who suffered under Diocletian.
11-10.name: Orestes the Physician

11-10.bio:
Saint Nonnus was a monk of Tabenna who was made bishop of Heliopolis, and later of Edessa, in the fifth century. He is remembered chiefly for his preaching at Antioch, which brought the famous actress Pelagia to repentance.

He baptized her, and she went on to live as an ascetic on the Mount of Olives. Nonnus reposed in peace.
11-10.desc: Saint Nonnus, Bishop of Heliopolis, who converted and baptized Saint Pelagia.
11-10.name: Nonnus of Heliopolis

11-10.bio:
Venerable Theosterictus was abbot of the monastery of Symbola on the Bithynian Olympus in the ninth century. Tradition relates that he suffered for the veneration of the holy icons during the iconoclast persecution.

He is also remembered as the author of the Small Paraclesis canon to the Theotokos according to some traditions, and reposed in peace.
11-10.desc: Venerable Theosterictus, abbot of the monastery of Symbola on Mount Olympus in Bithynia.
11-10.name: Theosterictus of Symbola

11-10.bio:
Saint Milos was a bishop in Persia in the fourth century, known as a wonderworker. When his flock rejected his preaching he travelled to Jerusalem and Egypt, and on his return continued to labour for the Gospel.

During the persecution of King Shapur he was arrested with two disciples and put to death by the sword.
11-10.desc: Hieromartyr Milos, Bishop in Persia, and his two disciples.
11-10.name: Milos the Wonderworker

11-11.bio:
The holy martyr Victor was a Christian soldier who suffered for Christ in the second century, refusing to sacrifice to idols and enduring cruel tortures with unshaken faith. Stephanida, the young wife of another soldier, saw his endurance, confessed Christ openly, and was put to death with him.

The Church honors them together as witnesses whose courage under torment revealed the power of grace. They are commemorated on November 11.
11-11.name: Victor and Stephanida

11-11.bio:
Saint Menas was an Egyptian soldier in the Roman army in the late third century. When Diocletian's persecution began he left the army and lived in the mountains in prayer, then returned to Kotyaion in Phrygia and openly confessed Christ during the games.

After cruel tortures he was beheaded. His relics were brought to Egypt, where his shrine at Abu Mena became one of the great pilgrimage centres of the ancient world; he is patron of Heraklion in Crete.
11-11.desc: Holy Great Martyr Menas of Egypt, the soldier martyred at Kotyaion, patron of Heraklion.
11-11.name: Menas the Great Martyr

11-11.bio:
Saint Vincent was a deacon of Saragossa in Spain and a disciple of Bishop Valerius. During the persecution of Diocletian he was brought to Valencia, where he boldly confessed Christ before the governor Dacian.

He endured terrible tortures on the rack and the gridiron and died in prison, one of the most celebrated martyrs of the West.
11-11.desc: Hieromartyr Vincent the Deacon of Saragossa, martyred at Valencia under Diocletian.
11-11.name: Vincent the Deacon

11-11.bio:
Saint Theodore was born in Constantinople in 759 and became abbot of the monastery of the Studion, which he made a model of monastic order. He suffered repeated exile and imprisonment, first for opposing the uncanonical marriage of the emperor and later for defending the veneration of the holy icons.

He wrote extensively on the monastic life and the icons, composed many hymns, and reposed in exile in 826.
11-11.desc: Venerable Theodore the Confessor, Abbot of the Studion monastery and defender of the holy icons.
11-11.name: Theodore the Studite

11-11.bio:
Blessed Maximus lived in Moscow in the fifteenth century as a fool for Christ, going about without shelter in every season and rebuking the sins of rich and poor alike. He reposed in 1434.

Many miracles were recorded at his tomb, and a church in Moscow bears his name.
11-11.desc: Blessed Maximus, Fool-for-Christ and Wonderworker of Moscow.
11-11.name: Maximus of Moscow

11-12.bio:
St. John the Merciful, a native of Cyprus, became Patriarch of Alexandria in the early seventh century. He earned his title by boundless almsgiving: he called the poor his masters, kept a register of the needy of the city, and poured out the wealth of the Church in feeding, clothing, and ransoming all who came to him, trusting that God would never be outgiven.

He reposed in peace in his homeland of Cyprus, and his example remains the Church's great icon of mercy toward the poor. He is commemorated on November 12.
11-12.name: John the Merciful

11-12.bio:
Saint Nilus was a high official in Constantinople and a disciple of Saint John Chrysostom. By agreement with his wife he left the world and settled with his son Theodoulos on Mount Sinai, where he lived as an ascetic.

He wrote many letters and treatises on the spiritual life which remain among the classics of Orthodox ascetical literature, and reposed in the fifth century.
11-12.desc: Venerable Nilus the Ascetic of Sinai, disciple of Saint John Chrysostom and spiritual writer.
11-12.name: Nilus of Sinai

11-12.bio:
Saint Nilus was born in the Peloponnese in the seventeenth century and became a monk on Mount Athos, living in a cave near the Great Lavra in strict asceticism. After his repose in 1651 fragrant myrrh flowed from his relics, from which he takes his name.

He is venerated on Athos as a great ascetic, and revelations attributed to him were recorded by later monks.
11-12.desc: Venerable Nilus the Myrrhgusher of Mount Athos.
11-12.name: Nilus the Myrrhgusher

11-12.bio:
Saint Martin was born in Pannonia in the fourth century and served in the Roman army. The famous story relates that as a catechumen he cut his cloak in half to clothe a freezing beggar, and that night saw Christ wearing the piece he had given away.

After his baptism he became a disciple of Saint Hilary of Poitiers, founded the first monastery in Gaul and was made Bishop of Tours, where he laboured for the conversion of the countryside and reposed in 397.
11-12.desc: Saint Martin the Merciful, Bishop of Tours, the soldier who shared his cloak with a beggar.
11-12.name: Martin of Tours

11-12.bio:
The Prophet Ahijah of Shiloh lived in the days of King Solomon and his son Rehoboam. As recorded in the Books of Kings, he foretold to Jeroboam that he would rule over ten tribes of Israel, and later prophesied the downfall of Jeroboam's house for its idolatry.

He reposed in peace.
11-12.desc: Holy Prophet Ahijah the Shilonite, who foretold the division of the kingdom of Israel.
11-12.name: Ahijah the Prophet

11-12.bio:
Saint Sabbas was born at Nigde in Cappadocia and earned his living as a tradesman in Constantinople. Tradition relates that after a dispute he was falsely accused before the Ottoman authorities and pressed to convert to Islam.

He refused and was beheaded in Constantinople in 1726.
11-12.desc: Holy New Martyr Sabbas Nigdelis of Nigde in Cappadocia, martyred in Constantinople in 1726.
11-12.name: Sabbas Nigdelis

11-12.bio:
The holy martyrs Zebinas, Germanos, Nikephoros and Antoninus suffered at Caesarea in Palestine under Maximian. They presented themselves before the governor and openly confessed Christ, and were beheaded.

The virgin Manatho of Scythopolis was martyred at the same time, being burned alive.
11-12.desc: Holy Martyrs Zebinas, Germanos, Nikephoros and Antoninus, with the Virgin Manatho, at Caesarea in Palestine.
11-12.name: Zebinas, Germanos, Nikephoros and Antoninus

11-13.bio:
St. John Chrysostom, the golden-mouthed preacher, was Archbishop of Constantinople at the turn of the fifth century. The greatest homilist of the Church, he expounded the Scriptures to his flock, defended the poor, and rebuked the powerful without fear, for which he was twice driven into exile; he died on the road in exile, with the words Glory to God for all things on his lips.

The Divine Liturgy most often celebrated in the Orthodox Church bears his name, and he is counted among the Three Holy Hierarchs. His repose is commemorated on November 13.
11-13.name: John Chrysostom (repose)

11-13.bio:
Saint Damaskenos was born in Galata of Constantinople and became a monk. Tradition relates that after a lapse he repented and, seeking to make amends, publicly confessed Christ before the Ottoman authorities.

He was beheaded in Constantinople in 1681.
11-13.desc: Holy New Monk-Martyr Damaskenos of Constantinople, martyred in 1681.
11-13.name: Damaskenos the New Martyr

11-14.bio:
The holy apostle Philip, one of the Twelve, was from Bethsaida of Galilee, the city of Peter and Andrew. Called by the Lord Himself, he brought Nathanael to Christ with the words Come and see, and in the Gospel of John he asks the Lord to show the disciples the Father. After Pentecost he preached the Gospel in Asia Minor and, according to tradition, ended his life as a martyr at Hierapolis.

The Nativity Fast begins the day after his feast, which is why it is called St. Philip's Fast in many lands. He is commemorated on November 14.
11-14.desc: Holy Apostle Philip, one of the Twelve.
11-14.name: Philip the Apostle

11-14.bio:
Saint Gregory Palamas was born in Constantinople in 1296 and became a monk on Mount Athos. In the fourteenth century he defended the hesychast monks against the attacks of Barlaam of Calabria, teaching that the faithful may truly share in the uncreated energies of God.

His teaching was confirmed by councils in Constantinople, and he was made Archbishop of Thessaloniki. He reposed in 1359 and is also honoured on the second Sunday of Great Lent.
11-14.desc: Saint Gregory Palamas, Archbishop of Thessaloniki, defender of hesychast prayer and the uncreated light.
11-14.name: Gregory Palamas

11-14.bio:
Saint Constantine was born on the island of Hydra and as a young man in Rhodes was drawn into the service of the Ottoman governor and renounced his faith. Overcome by remorse, he returned to the Church, spent time on Mount Athos in repentance, and went back to Rhodes to confess Christ openly.

He was imprisoned, tortured and hanged in 1800. His relics are venerated on Hydra.
11-14.desc: Holy New Martyr Constantine of Hydra, martyred at Rhodes in 1800.
11-14.name: Constantine of Hydra

11-14.bio:
According to the synaxarion of Saint Nikodemos, after the martyrdom of the Apostle Philip at Hierapolis, his companion the Apostle Bartholomew ordained Stachys as bishop of that city.

He is commemorated together with the Apostle Philip.
11-14.desc: Saint Stachys, Bishop of Hierapolis, ordained by the Apostle Bartholomew.
11-14.name: Stachys of Hierapolis

11-14.bio:
Tradition relates that Saint Euphemianos was among the Greeks who set out on the Second Crusade in the twelfth century and, when it dispersed, settled in Cyprus. He lived as a hermit near the village of Lysi, devoting himself to prayer.

He was known for his miracles, and a church near Lysi preserved his memory.
11-14.desc: Venerable Euphemianos the Wonderworker, hermit of Lysi in Cyprus.
11-14.name: Euphemianos of Cyprus

11-15.bio:
The holy confessors Gurias and Samonas were Christians of Edessa in Mesopotamia who suffered for Christ in the persecutions of the early fourth century, enduring imprisonment and torture before being put to death. The deacon Abibus, martyred in the same city some years later, is honored with them.

The three are venerated in Edessa and throughout the Church as protectors of the wronged, and many faithful have sought their intercession in distress. They are commemorated on November 15.
11-15.desc: Holy Martyrs Gourias, Samonas and Abibus.
11-15.name: Gurias and Samonas

11-15.bio:
Saint Elpidios was a senator who confessed Christ before Julian the Apostate and was condemned with his companions Marcellus and Eustochios. Tradition relates that they were tortured and finally burned.

They are commemorated together as martyrs of the fourth century.
11-15.desc: Holy Martyrs Elpidios, Marcellus and Eustochios, who suffered under Julian the Apostate.
11-15.name: Elpidios, Marcellus and Eustochios

11-15.bio:
Saint Kyntion was Bishop of Seleucia and is honoured in the synaxarion for his holy life. Tradition relates that he reposed in peace after governing his see with wisdom.

No further details of his life have been preserved.
11-15.name: Kyntion of Seleucia

11-15.bio:
The Emperor Justinian ruled the Byzantine Empire in the sixth century and is remembered for the building of the Great Church of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, for his codification of Roman law and for his defence of the Orthodox faith. His wife Theodora was his close counsellor and known for her charity.

The Church honours them together as pious rulers.
11-15.desc: Saints Justinian the Emperor and Theodora the Empress, builders of Hagia Sophia.
11-15.name: Justinian and Theodora

11-15.bio:
Saint Demetrios was a Christian of the village of Dabuda in Thrace. According to the synaxarion he was seized during the persecution of Maximian and, refusing to sacrifice, was beheaded.

He is distinct from the Great Martyr Demetrios of Thessaloniki.
11-15.desc: Holy Martyr Demetrios of Dabuda in Thrace.
11-15.name: Demetrios of Thrace

11-15.bio:
Saint Thomas II was Patriarch of Constantinople in the seventh century. The synaxarion honours him for his virtue and for governing the Church in peace during a troubled time.

He reposed in peace.
11-15.desc: Saint Thomas II the New, Patriarch of Constantinople.
11-15.name: Thomas II of Constantinople

11-16.bio:
The holy apostle and evangelist Matthew was a tax collector at Capernaum when the Lord called him with the words Follow me; he rose at once, left everything, and made a feast for Christ in his house. One of the Twelve, he wrote the first of the four Gospels, setting forth Christ as the fulfillment of the Law and the Prophets.

After Pentecost he preached the Gospel to many peoples and, according to tradition, ended his life in martyrdom. He is commemorated on November 16.
11-16.name: Matthew the Evangelist

11-16.bio:
Tradition relates that Iphigenia was a princess of Ethiopia who was healed and baptized by the Apostle Matthew and dedicated herself to Christ as a virgin, gathering other maidens around her.

When a later king sought to marry her she refused, and she is honoured as a virgin martyr, commemorated with the Apostle and Evangelist Matthew.
11-16.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Iphigenia of Ethiopia, converted by the Apostle Matthew.
11-16.name: Iphigenia the Virgin Martyr

11-16.bio:
Saint Philoumenos was born in Cyprus in 1913 and became a monk of the Jerusalem Patriarchate. In 1979 he was appointed guardian of the shrine of Jacob's Well at Nablus, where the Lord spoke with the Samaritan woman.

On 29 November 1979 (16 November on the old calendar) he was attacked and killed while at prayer in the church. His relics were found incorrupt, and he was glorified by the Patriarchate of Jerusalem in 2009.
11-16.desc: Holy New Hieromartyr Philoumenos of Cyprus, guardian of Jacob's Well, martyred in 1979.
11-16.name: Philoumenos of Jacob's Well

11-17.bio:
St. Gregory the Wonderworker was Bishop of Neocaesarea in Pontus in the third century. A student of philosophy who was won to Christ, he received the episcopate of a city with only a handful of Christians; through his preaching and the many miracles God worked through him, it is said that at his death only a handful of pagans remained.

He is one of the earliest saints to bear the title Wonderworker, and the Fathers of Cappadocia honored his memory and his teaching. He is commemorated on November 17.
11-17.desc: Bishop Gregory the Wonderworker of Neocaesarea.
11-17.name: Gregory the Wonderworker

11-17.bio:
Saint Gennadios was Patriarch of Constantinople in the fifth century, a learned theologian and reformer of the clergy who is remembered for his holiness of life and his miracles. Saint Maximos III was Patriarch in the fifteenth century, shortly after the fall of the City, and was known for his pastoral care of the enslaved flock.

The two are commemorated together on this day.
11-17.desc: Saints Gennadios I and Maximos III, Patriarchs of Constantinople.
11-17.name: Gennadios and Maximos of Constantinople

11-17.bio:
Saint Lazarus was a monk and icon painter in Constantinople in the ninth century. During the iconoclast persecution of the Emperor Theophilos he continued to paint icons and was imprisoned and tortured; tradition relates that his hands were burned with hot irons.

After the restoration of the icons he painted the image of Christ over the Chalke gate of the palace and reposed in peace.
11-17.desc: Venerable Lazarus the Iconographer of Constantinople, confessor under the iconoclasts.
11-17.name: Lazarus the Iconographer

11-17.bio:
Tradition relates that John, a pious man of Constantinople, prayed to be shown someone with whom he would share eternal life, and was directed to Zacharias, a humble shoemaker. He found that Zacharias and his wife lived in poverty, giving away most of their earnings and keeping a secret vow of chastity.

The two are honoured together as examples of hidden holiness among laypeople.
11-17.desc: Righteous Zacharias the Shoemaker and John, who lived hidden lives of virtue in Constantinople.
11-17.name: Zacharias the Shoemaker and John

11-17.bio:
Venerable Gennadios was the steward of the Vatopedi monastery on Mount Athos in the fourteenth century. Tradition relates that when the monastery's oil ran out he wished to stop supplying the brethren, but the abbot ordered him to trust in the Theotokos, and the empty jar was found overflowing.

The icon before which this took place is venerated at Vatopedi as the Elaiovrytissa, the Oil-Flowing.
11-17.desc: Venerable Gennadios of Vatopedi, steward of the monastery, witness of the miracle of the oil.
11-17.name: Gennadios of Vatopedi

11-17.bio:
Venerable Nikon came as a young man to Saint Sergius of Radonezh and became his closest disciple, succeeding him as abbot of the Holy Trinity monastery. After the monastery was burned by the Tatars he rebuilt it and had the relics of Saint Sergius uncovered.

He commissioned Andrei Rublev to paint the famous icon of the Holy Trinity, and reposed in 1426.
11-17.desc: Venerable Nikon, Abbot of Radonezh, disciple and successor of Saint Sergius.
11-17.name: Nikon of Radonezh

11-18.bio:
The holy martyr Plato was a young Christian of Ancyra in Galatia who suffered in the persecutions at the beginning of the fourth century. Brought before the governor, he refused every inducement to deny Christ, answered his judges with boldness and wisdom, and after enduring cruel tortures was beheaded.

The Church remembers him as a fearless young confessor whose witness strengthened the faithful of his city. He is commemorated on November 18.
11-18.name: Plato of Ancyra

11-18.bio:
Saint Romanos was a deacon of Caesarea in Palestine who was in Antioch during the persecution of Diocletian. Seeing Christians going to offer sacrifice, he exhorted them to stand firm and was arrested. Tradition relates that when the governor mocked him, Romanos called a small boy, Barulas, who confessed Christ and was beheaded.

Romanos had his tongue cut out, yet continued to praise God, and was finally strangled in prison.
11-18.desc: Holy Martyrs Romanos the Deacon of Caesarea and the child Barulas, martyred at Antioch.
11-18.name: Romanos the Deacon and Barulas

11-18.bio:
Saint Anastasios was a young man of Paramythia in Epirus. Tradition relates that when he defended his sister from an Ottoman official, he was arrested and pressed to convert to Islam.

He refused steadfastly and was beheaded in 1750. His memory is kept in Epirus.
11-18.desc: Holy New Martyr Anastasios of Paramythia in Epirus, martyred in 1750.
11-18.name: Anastasios of Paramythia

11-18.bio:
Saint Zacchaeus was a deacon of the church of Gadara and Alphaeus a reader of Caesarea. During the persecution of Diocletian they were arrested, Zacchaeus for his open confession and Alphaeus for exhorting Christians not to sacrifice.

After tortures both were beheaded at Caesarea in Palestine.
11-18.desc: Holy Martyrs Zacchaeus the Deacon of Gadara and Alphaeus the Reader, at Caesarea in Palestine.
11-18.name: Zacchaeus and Alphaeus

11-19.bio:
The holy prophet Abdias, called Obadiah in the Hebrew Scriptures, is one of the twelve minor prophets, and his book is the shortest in the Old Testament. In it he pronounces the judgment of God upon Edom for its pride and its violence against Israel, and he foretells the day of the Lord and the deliverance that shall be upon Mount Zion.

The Church honors him among the prophets who prepared the way for the coming of Christ. He is commemorated on November 19.
11-19.name: Abdias the Prophet

11-19.bio:
Saint Barlaam was an elderly Christian of Caesarea in Cappadocia during the persecution of Diocletian. Tradition relates that the governor placed burning coals and incense on his open palm over a pagan altar, hoping he would drop them and appear to sacrifice.

Barlaam held his hand steady until it burned through, and died confessing Christ. Saints Basil the Great and John Chrysostom preached homilies in his honour.
11-19.desc: Holy Martyr Barlaam of Caesarea in Cappadocia, who held burning coals in his hand rather than sacrifice.
11-19.name: Barlaam of Caesarea

11-19.bio:
Saint Heliodoros was a Christian of Magydos in Pamphylia during the reign of Aurelian. Arrested for his faith, he was subjected to many tortures, which tradition relates he bore with such courage that some of his torturers believed.

He was finally beheaded.
11-19.desc: Holy Martyr Heliodoros of Magydos in Pamphylia.
11-19.name: Heliodoros of Magydos

11-19.bio:
Saint Azes was a soldier of Isauria during the persecution of Diocletian who left the army to live in prayer and was known for working miracles. Arrested and brought to the governor, he was tortured for his faith.

Tradition relates that a hundred and fifty soldiers sent to guard him believed in Christ through his miracles and were martyred with him.
11-19.desc: Holy Martyr Azes the Wonderworker of Isauria and the 150 soldiers martyred with him.
11-19.name: Azes and the 150 soldiers

11-19.bio:
The holy martyrs Anthimos, Thallelaios, Christopher and Euphemia with her children, and Pancharios, are commemorated together in the synaxarion. Tradition records that they suffered for Christ by the sword.

No further details of their lives are preserved.
11-19.desc: Holy Martyrs Anthimos, Thallelaios, Christopher, Euphemia and her children, and Pancharios.
11-19.name: Anthimos, Thallelaios, Christopher and Euphemia

11-19.bio:
Saint Hilarion was born in Georgia in the ninth century and became a monk at an early age. He travelled to the Holy Land, Mount Olympus in Bithynia, Rome and Constantinople, living in prayer and working miracles.

He settled finally in Thessaloniki, where he reposed in peace in 875. His relics were later carried to Constantinople.
11-19.desc: Venerable Hilarion the Georgian, wonderworker, who reposed in Thessaloniki.
11-19.name: Hilarion the Iberian

11-19.bio:
Saint Philaret Drozdov was Metropolitan of Moscow for nearly half a century in the nineteenth century. A theologian and preacher of great learning, he composed the Catechism used throughout the Russian Church and oversaw the translation of the Bible into Russian.

He reposed in 1867 and was glorified in 1994.
11-19.desc: Saint Philaret Drozdov, Metropolitan of Moscow, theologian and author of the Catechism.
11-19.name: Philaret of Moscow

11-2.bio:
The holy martyrs Akindynos, Pegasios, Aphthonios, Elpidophoros, and Anempodistos were Christians of Persia who suffered in the fourth century, during a fierce persecution of the Church in that land. Refusing to deny Christ, they endured many torments and were put to death, and their steadfastness drew others to the faith.

The Church honors them as a company of confessors whose courage strengthened the persecuted Christians of Persia. They are commemorated on November 2.
11-2.desc: Holy Martyrs Acindynus, Pigasius and companions.
11-2.name: Akindynos and companions

11-2.bio:
The holy women martyrs Kyriaki, Domnina and Domna are commemorated together in the Church's calendar. The synaxarion records that they were put to death by the sword for confessing Christ.

No further details of their lives have been preserved.
11-2.desc: Holy Martyrs Kyriaki, Domnina and Domna, who suffered for Christ.
11-2.name: Kyriaki, Domnina and Domna

11-2.bio:
Venerable Marcian lived in the fourth century as a hermit in the desert of Chalcis near Cyrrhus in Syria. Of noble birth, he left the imperial court to live in a small cell, devoting himself to prayer, fasting and the study of Scripture.

Tradition relates that disciples gathered around him and that he was known for his discernment and humility, refusing to be ordained and asking that his burial place remain unknown.
11-2.desc: Venerable Marcian, hermit of the desert near Cyrrhus in Syria.
11-2.name: Marcian of Cyrrhus

11-2.bio:
The holy martyrs Eudoxios, Agapios, Atticus, Marinus, Oceanus, Eustratius, Carterius, Nicopolitianus, Styrax and Tobias suffered at Sebaste in Armenia. Eudoxios is said to have been a military commander who was denounced for his faith.

According to the synaxarion they were tortured and finally beheaded together during the persecution of Licinius.
11-2.desc: Holy Martyrs Eudoxios, Agapios and eight others who suffered at Sebaste.
11-2.name: Eudoxios, Agapios and companions

11-2.bio:
Saint Anthony was Archbishop of Thessaloniki in the ninth century. During the second period of iconoclasm he confessed the veneration of the holy icons and was persecuted, exiled and mistreated for his stand.

Tradition relates that he returned to his see after the restoration of Orthodoxy and reposed in peace.
11-2.desc: Saint Anthony the Confessor, Archbishop of Thessaloniki, who suffered for the holy icons.
11-2.name: Anthony of Thessaloniki

11-2.bio:
The new martyrs Lambros, Theodore and a third companion whose name is not recorded were merchants from the Peloponnese who had lived for a time in Ioannina. Returning home in 1786 they stopped at Vrachori, the present Agrinio, where a dispute with Ottoman tax collectors led to their arrest.

Pressed to deny their faith, they refused and were hanged. Their memory is kept in the Church of Greece as an example of lay confessors of the Ottoman period.
11-2.desc: Holy New Martyrs Lambros, Theodore and a third unnamed companion, hanged at Vrachori (Agrinio) in 1786.
11-2.name: Lambros and Theodore, New Martyrs of Agrinio

11-20.bio:
St. Proclos was a disciple of St. John Chrysostom and served as Patriarch of Constantinople in the fifth century. A gentle and eloquent shepherd, he taught the faith with clarity, honored the Theotokos in his celebrated homilies, and brought the relics of his teacher Chrysostom back to Constantinople with great solemnity, healing an old wound in the Church.

Tradition also connects his patriarchate with the establishment of the Trisagion hymn in the services of the Church. He reposed in peace and is commemorated on November 20.
11-20.desc: Patriarch of Constantinople, disciple of St. John Chrysostom.
11-20.name: Proclos of Constantinople

11-20.bio:
The holy martyrs Proclus and Hilarius suffered for Christ in the early centuries of the Church, during the Roman persecutions. Tradition relates that Proclus was seized first and endured torture with steadfastness, and that his witness moved his kinsman Hilarius to confess Christ openly; both were put to death for the faith.

The synaxaria preserve little more than their faithful confession, which the Church treasures as a seed of the Gospel. They are commemorated on November 20.
11-20.name: Proclus the Martyr

11-20.bio:
Saint Gregory was born in Irenopolis of the Isaurian Decapolis in the ninth century and became a monk, living as an ascetic in various places and travelling to Rome, Sicily and Thessaloniki. He preached against iconoclasm and was known for his miracles.

He reposed in Constantinople in 842. His relics are venerated at the Bistrita monastery in Romania.
11-20.desc: Venerable Gregory the Decapolite, ascetic and defender of the holy icons.
11-20.name: Gregory the Decapolite

11-20.bio:
Saint Dasius was a soldier at Dorostolum on the Danube during the reign of Diocletian. Chosen by lot to play the king in the pagan festival of Saturn, he refused to take part in the revelry and openly confessed Christ.

He was tortured and beheaded. His relics were later brought to Ancona in Italy.
11-20.desc: Holy Martyr Dasius, the soldier of Dorostolum who refused to play the king of the Saturnalia.
11-20.name: Dasius of Dorostolum

11-20.bio:
Saint Nerses was a bishop in Persia and Joseph his disciple, who was also a bishop. During the persecution of King Shapur II in the fourth century they were arrested with many clergy and laypeople for refusing to worship the sun.

They were beheaded, and the many men and women who suffered with them are commemorated on the same day.
11-20.desc: Hieromartyrs Nerses the Bishop and Joseph his disciple, with many others martyred in Persia.
11-20.name: Nerses and Joseph of Persia

11-20.bio:
Saints Eustathios, Thespesios and Anatolios were three brothers of Gangra who were converted with their parents and lived in Nicaea. During the persecution of Maximian they were arrested for their faith.

After tortures they were beheaded at Nicaea.
11-20.desc: Holy Martyrs Eustathios, Thespesios and Anatolios of Nicaea, three brothers.
11-20.name: Eustathios, Thespesios and Anatolios

11-20.bio:
Saint Sozomenos was a native of Karpasia in Cyprus who, tradition relates, lived before the Frankish occupation of the island. Well educated, he left his home as a young man to live in a cave as a hermit, devoting himself to prayer.

He was known for his miracles, and his cave church near Potamia remains a place of veneration in Cyprus.
11-20.desc: Venerable Sozomenos the Wonderworker, hermit of Karpasia in Cyprus.
11-20.name: Sozomenos of Cyprus

11-21.bio:
The Entry of the Theotokos into the Temple, kept on November 21, commemorates the day the child Mary, at the age of three, was brought by her parents Joachim and Anna to the Temple in Jerusalem in fulfillment of their vow. According to tradition she was received by the priest Zacharias and dwelt in the Temple, nourished in prayer and prepared to become the living temple of God.

The feast celebrates the dedication of the Mother of God wholly to the Lord from childhood. Falling near the beginning of the Nativity Fast, it points ahead to the mystery of the Incarnation.
11-21.desc: The Entry of our Most Holy Lady the Theotokos into the Temple.
11-21.name: Entry of the Theotokos into the Temple

11-21.bio:
Blessed Procopius lived in the town of Vyatka in Russia in the seventeenth century. After being struck by lightning as a boy he was healed at a monastery and took up the ascetic life of a fool for Christ, going barefoot in winter and bearing insults with patience.

He was known for his gift of foresight and reposed in 1627.
11-21.name: Procopius of Vyatka

11-22.bio:
The holy apostle Philemon, one of the Seventy, was a Christian of Colossae and the recipient of the Apostle Paul's epistle that bears his name, in which Paul pleads for the runaway slave Onesimus as for a beloved brother. His household was a gathering place for the church of his city.

Tradition holds that he served the Gospel in Asia Minor and ended his life as a martyr, together with his wife Apphia. He is commemorated on November 22.
11-22.name: Philemon the Apostle

11-22.bio:
Saint Cecilia was a Roman noblewoman of the third century who had dedicated herself to Christ. Married against her will to the pagan Valerian, she persuaded him to respect her vow, and he and his brother Tiburtius were baptized and became zealous Christians.

The two brothers were beheaded, and Cecilia, after surviving an attempt to suffocate her in her bath, was struck with the sword and died confessing Christ. She is honoured in the West as patroness of music.
11-22.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Cecilia of Rome with her husband Valerian, his brother Tiburtius and the martyr Maximus.
11-22.name: Cecilia, Valerian and Tiburtius

11-22.bio:
Saint Iakovos Tsalikis was born in Asia Minor in 1920 and came to Euboea as a refugee child. He became a monk at the monastery of Saint David the Elder, where he served as abbot for many years, living in great asceticism and known for his humility, discernment and the healings worked through his prayers.

He reposed in 1991 and was glorified by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 2017.
11-22.desc: Venerable Iakovos Tsalikis, abbot of the monastery of Saint David in Euboea, glorified in 2017.
11-22.name: Iakovos of Evia

11-22.bio:
Saint Kallistos Xanthopoulos was a monk of Mount Athos and a disciple of the hesychast tradition of Saint Gregory of Sinai. Together with his companion Ignatios he composed the treatise on the spiritual life included in the Philokalia.

He was briefly Patriarch of Constantinople at the end of the fourteenth century and reposed in peace.
11-22.desc: Saint Kallistos II Xanthopoulos, Patriarch of Constantinople and hesychast writer.
11-22.name: Kallistos II of Constantinople

11-22.bio:
Saint Procopius was a reader and interpreter of the church of Scythopolis who was brought to Caesarea in Palestine at the beginning of Diocletian's persecution. Refusing to sacrifice to the emperors, he confessed Christ before the governor.

He was beheaded, the first of the martyrs of Palestine recorded by Eusebius.
11-22.desc: Holy Martyr Procopius the Reader of Caesarea in Palestine.
11-22.name: Procopius the Reader

11-22.bio:
Saint Menignus was a fuller of Parium on the Hellespont during the persecution of Decius. Tradition relates that he tore up an imperial edict against the Christians and openly confessed Christ.

After tortures he was beheaded.
11-22.desc: Holy Martyr Menignus the Fuller of Parium.
11-22.name: Menignus the Fuller

11-22.bio:
Saint Clement was a disciple of Saints Cyril and Methodios and, after their death, laboured in Bulgaria, where he was made bishop and founded a school at Ochrid that trained thousands of clergy and teachers in the Slavonic language.

He reposed in 916 and is honoured with his companions Nahum, Sabbas, Gorazd and Angelar as one of the Seven Apostles of the Slavs.
11-22.desc: Saint Clement of Ochrid, Equal to the Apostles, disciple of Saints Cyril and Methodios and enlightener of the Slavs.
11-22.name: Clement of Ochrid

11-23.bio:
St. Amphilochios was Bishop of Iconium in the fourth century, a kinsman and friend of the great Cappadocian Fathers; St. Basil the Great addressed to him important letters on the canons and dedicated to him his treatise on the Holy Spirit. He labored against the Arian heresy and took part in the Second Ecumenical Council at Constantinople.

A wise shepherd and defender of the divinity of the Son and the Spirit, he reposed in peace in old age. He is commemorated on November 23.
11-23.name: Amphilochios of Iconium

11-23.bio:
Saint Gregory was born near Agrigentum in Sicily in the sixth century and travelled widely in the East, studying in Jerusalem, Antioch and Constantinople, before being made bishop of his native city. He was falsely accused by enemies and imprisoned in Rome, but was vindicated and restored.

He wrote a commentary on Ecclesiastes and reposed in peace.
11-23.desc: Saint Gregory, Bishop of Agrigentum in Sicily.
11-23.name: Gregory of Agrigentum

11-23.bio:
Saint Alexander was Prince of Novgorod in the thirteenth century and won his name by his victory over the Swedes on the Neva in 1240. He defended Russia against the Teutonic Knights while dealing prudently with the Mongol overlords to spare his people.

He received the monastic schema before his death in 1263 and is one of the most venerated saints of Russia.
11-23.desc: Saint Alexander Nevsky, Grand Prince of Novgorod and Vladimir, defender of Orthodox Russia.
11-23.name: Alexander Nevsky

11-23.bio:
Saint Sisinios was Bishop of Cyzicus who suffered for the faith during the persecution of Diocletian. Tradition relates that he was tortured and confessed Christ, and after the peace of the Church reposed in his see.

He is honoured as a confessor.
11-23.desc: Saint Sisinios the Confessor, Bishop of Cyzicus.
11-23.name: Sisinios of Cyzicus

11-23.bio:
Saint Metrophanes was a married parish priest who became a monk after the death of his wife and in 1682 was consecrated the first Bishop of Voronezh. He was known for his care of the poor, his building of churches and his frank counsel to Tsar Peter the Great.

He reposed in 1703 in the schema with the name Macarius, and his relics were found incorrupt.
11-23.desc: Saint Metrophanes, first Bishop of Voronezh.
11-23.name: Metrophanes of Voronezh

11-23.bio:
Saint Dionysios was a disciple of Saint Mark Eugenikos and became Patriarch of Constantinople twice in the fifteenth century, in the difficult years after the fall of the City. He was slandered and deposed but vindicated, and later withdrew to the Eikosifoinissa monastery.

He reposed there in peace, and his relics are venerated at the monastery.
11-23.desc: Saint Dionysios I, Patriarch of Constantinople.
11-23.name: Dionysios I of Constantinople

11-24.bio:
St. Clement was Bishop of Rome at the end of the first century, a man of the apostolic generation whom tradition associates with the companions of the Apostles Peter and Paul. His epistle to the Corinthians, written to heal division in that church, is among the most precious writings of the early Church. Exiled for the faith to the region of the Crimea, he labored among the faithful there and was martyred by drowning.

The Church honors him as an apostolic father and hieromartyr whose words still teach concord and humility. He is commemorated on November 24.
11-24.desc: Pope Clement I of Rome, martyr.
11-24.name: Clement of Rome

11-24.bio:
Saint Peter became Archbishop of Alexandria in 300 and guided the Church through the persecution of Diocletian and his successors. He opposed the schism of Meletius and the early errors of Arius, whom he excommunicated.

Tradition relates that he was beheaded in 311 by order of Maximinus, and that before his death he saw Christ in a vision with His garment torn, a sign of the coming Arian division.
11-24.desc: Hieromartyr Peter, Archbishop of Alexandria, the last martyr of the great persecution.
11-24.name: Peter of Alexandria

11-24.bio:
Saint Hermogenes was Bishop of Agrigentum in Sicily. The synaxarion records that he governed his flock with wisdom and reposed in peace.

No further details of his life are preserved.
11-24.desc: Saint Hermogenes, Bishop of Agrigentum in Sicily.
11-24.name: Hermogenes of Agrigentum

11-24.bio:
Venerable Malchus is honoured in the synaxarion as a monk who reposed in peace. Tradition identifies him with the Syrian monk whose story of captivity among the desert nomads and faithful return to his monastery was recorded by Saint Jerome.

No other details are preserved.
11-24.name: Malchus the Venerable

11-24.bio:
Venerable Karion was a monk of Scetis in Egypt and the father of Venerable Zacharias, who followed him into the desert as a boy. The Evergetinos preserves his saying that a man who keeps a child with him in the desert cannot advance to the higher measures of virtue.

He reposed in peace.
11-24.desc: Venerable Karion of Egypt, father of Venerable Zacharias.
11-24.name: Karion the Venerable

11-24.bio:
Saint Mercurius was a soldier of Smolensk in the thirteenth century. Tradition relates that the Theotokos appeared to him and sent him against the Tatar army approaching the city; he slew their champion and put them to flight, but was himself beheaded.

He is venerated as the protector of Smolensk.
11-24.desc: Holy Martyr Mercurius of Smolensk, who died defending the city from the Tatars.
11-24.name: Mercurius of Smolensk

11-24.bio:
Saint Chrysogonos was a Christian of Rome and the spiritual teacher of the Great Martyr Anastasia. Imprisoned under Diocletian, he strengthened her by his letters.

He was taken to Aquileia and beheaded, and his memory is kept with that of Saint Anastasia.
11-24.desc: Holy Martyr Chrysogonos, teacher of Saint Anastasia, martyred at Aquileia.
11-24.name: Chrysogonos the Martyr

11-25.bio:
St. Catherine the Great Martyr was a noble and brilliantly educated maiden of Alexandria, martyred at the beginning of the fourth century. According to tradition, she confessed Christ before the emperor and bested in debate the philosophers gathered to refute her, leading many to the faith. After torture on the wheel, which was broken by grace, she was beheaded.

Her relics rest at the great monastery of Sinai that bears her name. She is honored as a patroness of learning and students, and her feast, kept on November 25 in some traditions and November 25 in others, is a cherished name day for Katerina.
11-25.name: Catherine the Great Martyr

11-25.bio:
Saint Mercurius was a Scythian officer in the Roman army who, according to tradition, was granted victory in battle by an angel and afterwards confessed Christ before the Emperor Decius. He was subjected to cruel tortures and beheaded at Caesarea in Cappadocia.

A later tradition relates that Saint Basil the Great saw him in a vision being sent to slay Julian the Apostate. He is greatly venerated in Greece and Egypt.
11-25.desc: Holy Great Martyr Mercurius of Caesarea in Cappadocia, the soldier martyred under Decius.
11-25.name: Mercurius the Great Martyr

11-25.bio:
Venerable Peter was born in Galatia and, according to Theodoret of Cyrrhus, left home at the age of seven to live as an ascetic. He settled in a tomb near Antioch where he lived for many years in silence and prayer.

He was known for his miracles and reposed at a great age in the fifth century.
11-25.desc: Venerable Peter the Hesychast of Galatia, who lived as an ascetic from childhood.
11-25.name: Peter the Hesychast

11-25.bio:
Saint Augusta was the wife of the emperor Maxentius. Tradition relates that she visited Saint Catherine in prison, was converted by her and confessed Christ before her husband.

She was tortured and beheaded, and is commemorated with the Great Martyr Catherine.
11-25.desc: Holy Martyr Augusta the Empress, converted by Saint Catherine.
11-25.name: Augusta the Empress

11-25.bio:
Saint Porphyrios was a general of the emperor Maxentius who, together with two hundred soldiers, believed in Christ through the witness of Saint Catherine and the Empress Augusta.

They confessed their faith before the emperor and were beheaded.
11-25.desc: Holy Martyr Porphyrios the General and the 200 soldiers martyred with him.
11-25.name: Porphyrios the General

11-25.bio:
Tradition relates that the emperor Maxentius summoned the most learned philosophers of the empire to dispute with Saint Catherine. Defeated by her wisdom, they confessed Christ.

They were burned alive by order of the emperor and are commemorated with the Great Martyr.
11-25.desc: The 150 philosophers and rhetors converted by Saint Catherine and martyred by fire.
11-25.name: The 150 Rhetors

11-26.bio:
Venerable Alypios the Stylite was an ascetic of Paphlagonia in Asia Minor who embraced the rare and severe discipline of the pillar saints, standing upon a column in unceasing prayer, exposed to heat and frost, for many decades. From his pillar he taught and consoled the many who came to him, and monastic communities gathered nearby under his care.

He reposed in extreme old age, having endured his ascetic struggle to the end even when his body failed. He is commemorated on November 26.
11-26.name: Alypios Stylites

11-26.bio:
Saint Stylianos was born in Paphlagonia in Asia Minor and, after giving his inheritance to the poor, lived as a hermit in a cave, devoting himself to prayer and asceticism. Tradition relates that he was granted the gift of healing, and that he had a special love for children.

Mothers brought their sick children to him and childless couples sought his prayers. He reposed in peace and is venerated throughout Greece as the protector of infants and children.
11-26.desc: Venerable Stylianos of Paphlagonia, hermit and protector of children.
11-26.name: Stylianos of Paphlagonia

11-26.bio:
Saint Nikon was born in Pontus in the tenth century and became a monk. He travelled through Asia Minor, Crete after its recovery from the Arabs, and the Peloponnese, preaching everywhere the single word Metanoeite, Repent, from which he took his name.

He settled at Sparta, where he built a church and reposed in peace around 998. He is the patron saint of Sparta.
11-26.desc: Venerable Nikon the Preacher of Repentance, apostle of Crete and the Peloponnese.
11-26.name: Nikon Metanoeite

11-26.bio:
Saint George was born on Chios and as a child was taken by Ottomans and raised as a Muslim, but returned to the Christian faith as a young man. Working at Kydonies in Asia Minor, he was recognized and denounced.

Refusing to deny Christ, he was hanged in 1807. His memory is kept on Chios and at Kydonies.
11-26.desc: Holy New Martyr George of Chios, martyred at Kydonies in 1807.
11-26.name: George of Chios

11-26.bio:
Saint Akakios was a young monk of Sinai who served a harsh elder with perfect obedience and patience, bearing daily abuse for nine years without complaint. Saint John Climacus tells his story in the Ladder of Divine Ascent.

After his death, when the elder was asked whether Akakios was truly dead, a voice from the tomb answered that one who practises obedience cannot die.
11-26.desc: Venerable Akakios of Sinai, the obedient disciple praised in the Ladder of Divine Ascent.
11-26.name: Akakios of the Ladder

11-26.bio:
Saint Sophianos was Bishop of Dryinoupolis in northern Epirus in the seventeenth century and is regarded as a forerunner of Saint Kosmas of Aitolia. He founded a school at the monastery of Saint Athanasios and travelled from village to village to strengthen the Christians against conversion to Islam.

He reposed in 1711, and his relics are venerated in Epirus.
11-26.desc: Saint Sophianos, Bishop of Dryinoupolis and Argyrokastro, teacher of the enslaved Greeks of Epirus.
11-26.name: Sophianos of Dryinoupolis

11-26.bio:
Venerable James lived as a hermit near Cyrrhus in Syria in the fifth century, in the open air without shelter, enduring heat and cold. Theodoret of Cyrrhus, who knew him, records his severe asceticism and his miracles.

He reposed in peace at an advanced age.
11-26.desc: Venerable James the Anchorite of Syria.
11-26.name: James the Solitary

11-27.bio:
The great martyr James the Persian was a Christian noble at the Persian court in the fifth century who, to please the king, denied Christ. Rebuked by the grief of his mother and his wife, he came to himself, repented, and confessed his faith before the king, for which he was condemned to a slow death by dismemberment; he endured it with prayer, and for this he is called the Cut-to-Pieces.

His repentance and endurance have made him one of the most venerated martyrs of the East. He is commemorated on November 27.
11-27.name: James the Persian

11-27.bio:
Saint Pinouphrios was abbot of a large monastery near Panephysis in Egypt in the fourth century. Fleeing the honour shown him, he twice left secretly, once to serve as an unknown novice in a monastery at Tabenna and once to Palestine, until he was recognized and brought back.

Saint John Cassian records his teaching on humility and renunciation. He reposed in peace.
11-27.desc: Venerable Pinouphrios of Egypt, the abbot who fled honour to live as an unknown novice.
11-27.name: Pinouphrios the Venerable

11-27.bio:
Venerable Nathanael was a monk of Nitria in Egypt in the fourth century. Tradition relates that after being tempted to leave his cell he resolved never to step across its threshold, and kept this rule for nearly forty years.

He reposed in peace.
11-27.desc: Venerable Nathanael of Nitria, who did not leave his cell for many years.
11-27.name: Nathanael the Venerable

11-27.bio:
Saint Gregory was born in Asia Minor in the thirteenth century and became a monk on Mount Sinai, later settling on Mount Athos, where he taught the practice of inner prayer to many disciples. Because of Turkish raids he withdrew to Paroria in Bulgaria, where he founded a monastery.

His writings on watchfulness and prayer are included in the Philokalia. He reposed in 1346.
11-27.desc: Venerable Gregory of Sinai, teacher of hesychast prayer on Athos and in Bulgaria.
11-27.name: Gregory of Sinai

11-27.bio:
Saint Theodosius was a Bulgarian monk who became a disciple of Saint Gregory of Sinai at Paroria and later founded the monastery of Kilifarevo near Trnovo, which became a centre of hesychast spirituality and learning. He defended Orthodoxy against heresies at councils in Trnovo.

He reposed in Constantinople in 1363.
11-27.desc: Venerable Theodosius of Trnovo, disciple of Gregory of Sinai and teacher of hesychasm in Bulgaria.
11-27.name: Theodosius of Trnovo

11-27.bio:
Saint Damaskenos was born in Thessaloniki in the sixteenth century and became a monk of the Studion. He was later Bishop of Liti and Rentini and Metropolitan of Naupaktos and Arta, and is remembered for his collection of homilies in the vernacular, the Thesauros, which was read throughout the Greek world under Ottoman rule.

He reposed in 1577 and was recognized as a saint by the Ecumenical Patriarchate.
11-27.desc: Saint Damaskenos the Studite, Bishop of Liti and Rentini, author of the Thesauros.
11-27.name: Damaskenos the Studite

11-27.bio:
Saint James was Bishop of Rostov in the fourteenth century. Tradition relates that when he spared a woman condemned to death, the people drove him from the city; he spread his mantle on the lake and floated across it, and founded a monastery on the far shore.

He reposed in 1392.
11-27.desc: Saint James the Wonderworker, Bishop of Rostov.
11-27.name: James of Rostov

11-28.bio:
The holy monk-martyr Stephen the Younger was an ascetic of Mount Auxentios near Constantinople in the eighth century, during the persecution of the holy icons. A monk from his youth and a guide to many, he refused to subscribe to the iconoclast council and boldly defended the veneration of the icons before the emperor himself; for this he was imprisoned, and he was finally killed by a mob in the streets of the capital.

He is honored as the foremost martyr of the iconoclast persecution. He is commemorated on November 28.
11-28.name: Stephen the Younger

11-28.bio:
Saint Irenarchos was an executioner at Sebaste in Armenia during the persecution of Diocletian. Seeing the courage of seven Christian women under torture, he believed in Christ and confessed openly.

He was tortured and beheaded together with the women and the priest Acacius who had baptized him.
11-28.desc: Holy Martyr Irenarchos and the seven women martyrs of Sebaste.
11-28.name: Irenarchos and the Seven Women

11-28.bio:
The fifteen hieromartyrs, among them the bishops Timothy and Theodore and the priests Eusebius, Peter and others, fled Nicaea during the persecution of Julian the Apostate and settled at Tiberiopolis in Macedonia, the present Strumica, where they preached the Gospel.

They were arrested and beheaded there, and their relics became a source of many healings.
11-28.desc: The Fifteen Hieromartyrs of Tiberiopolis (Strumica), martyred under Julian the Apostate.
11-28.name: Fifteen Hieromartyrs of Tiberiopolis

11-28.bio:
The monks and confessors Andrew, Peter, Auxentius, Basil, Gregory, another Gregory, John and many others suffered under the iconoclast emperor Constantine Copronymus for the veneration of the holy icons, at the same time as Saint Stephen the New.

They were imprisoned, tortured and put to death, and are commemorated together with him.
11-28.desc: Holy Martyrs Andrew, Peter, Auxentius, Basil, Gregory, John and others who suffered with Stephen the New.
11-28.greek: Ανδρέας, Πέτρος και οι συν αυτοίς
11-28.name: Andrew, Peter and companions of Stephen the New

11-28.bio:
Saint Anna was a nun in Constantinople who, according to tradition, was accused of association with Saint Stephen the New during the iconoclast persecution of Constantine Copronymus.

She was beaten to death for refusing to speak against him and the holy icons.
11-28.desc: Holy Monk-Martyr Anna, who suffered under the iconoclasts.
11-28.name: Anna the Monk-Martyr

11-28.bio:
Saint Theodore was the nephew of Saint Sergius of Radonezh and was tonsured by him as a boy. He founded the Simonov monastery in Moscow and was later made Archbishop of Rostov, where he was known as a builder of churches and an icon painter.

He reposed in 1394.
11-28.desc: Saint Theodore, Archbishop of Rostov, nephew of Saint Sergius of Radonezh.
11-28.name: Theodore of Rostov

11-29.bio:
The holy martyrs Paramon and Philomenus suffered for Christ in the third century, during the Roman persecutions. Tradition relates that Paramon, seeing a multitude of Christians being tortured for refusing to sacrifice to idols, openly confessed Christ and was put to death with them; Philomenus likewise sealed his confession with his blood.

The synaxaria preserve little beyond their faithful witness, which the Church holds in honor among the martyrs of that age. They are commemorated on November 29.
11-29.name: Paramon and Philomenus

11-29.bio:
Saint Dionysios was Bishop of Corinth in the second century and is known from Eusebius for his letters to many churches, which combined teaching with pastoral care. He is honoured in the synaxarion as a hieromartyr.

Tradition relates that his relics were later carried to Rome.
11-29.desc: Hieromartyr Dionysios, Bishop of Corinth in the second century.
11-29.name: Dionysios of Corinth

11-29.bio:
Saint Phaedros is honoured in the synaxarion as a martyr who was put to death by having boiling resin poured over him.

No other details of his life are preserved.
11-29.desc: Holy Martyr Phaedros, who was put to death with boiling resin.
11-29.name: Phaedros the Martyr

11-29.bio:
Saint Valerian is commemorated in the synaxarion as a martyr who suffered for Christ by the sword.

No further details of his life are preserved.
11-29.name: Valerian the Martyr

11-29.bio:
Saint Nicholas, Archbishop of Thessaloniki, is recorded in the Synaxarion of Constantinople and the Menaia as having reposed in peace on this day. Later lists of the bishops of Thessaloniki place him in the second century, though this dating is uncertain.

No details of his life are preserved.
11-29.name: Nicholas of Thessaloniki

11-29.bio:
Saint Abibus was one of the Thirteen Syrian Fathers who came to Georgia in the sixth century and was made Bishop of Nekresi. He preached against the Persian fire worship and, tradition relates, extinguished a sacred fire of the Zoroastrians.

He was arrested by the Persians and stoned to death.
11-29.desc: Hieromartyr Abibus, Bishop of Nekresi in Georgia, one of the Thirteen Syrian Fathers.
11-29.name: Abibus of Nekresi

11-29.bio:
On this day the Church of Greece commemorates together all the saints connected with Achaia in the northern Peloponnese, from the Apostle Andrew, who was martyred at Patras, to the martyrs and ascetics of later centuries.

The feast is kept on the eve of the Apostle Andrew's memory.
11-29.desc: Synaxis of all the saints of Achaia in the Peloponnese.
11-29.name: Synaxis of the Saints of Achaia

11-3.bio:
The holy hieromartyr Akepsimas was a bishop in Persia who suffered in the great persecution of the fourth century. Though advanced in years, he endured imprisonment and torture rather than worship the sun as his persecutors demanded, and he was put to death for his confession of Christ, together with the priest Joseph and the deacon Aeithalas.

The Church remembers him as a faithful shepherd who sealed a long life of service with martyrdom. He is commemorated on November 3.
11-3.name: Akepsimas of Persia

11-3.bio:
On this day the Church commemorates the consecration of the church of the Holy Great Martyr George in Lydda in Palestine and the placing of his holy relics there. Tradition relates that after his martyrdom in Nicomedia, the body of Saint George was carried to Lydda, his mother's homeland.

The feast is kept on the Greek calendar as a second commemoration of the Great Martyr, whose principal feast falls on April 23.
11-3.desc: Consecration of the church of the Great Martyr George at Lydda and the deposition of his relics there.
11-3.name: Consecration of the Church of George in Lydda

11-3.bio:
Saint George was a married priest of Neapolis in Cappadocia, the present Nevsehir, in the eighteenth century. He was known for his pastoral zeal among the Greek Christians of the region.

Tradition relates that he was denounced to the Ottoman authorities, refused to renounce his faith and was beheaded in 1797. His relics were venerated locally until the population exchange, when they were brought to Greece.
11-3.desc: Holy New Hieromartyr George, priest of Neapolis in Cappadocia, martyred in 1797.
11-3.name: George the New Hieromartyr of Neapolis

11-3.bio:
Venerable Akepsimas was a hermit of the region of Cyrrhus in Syria in the fourth century. Tradition relates that he shut himself in a small cell for some sixty years, receiving food through a narrow opening and speaking with no one.

Shortly before his death he was persuaded to accept ordination to the priesthood and reposed in peace soon afterwards. He is distinct from the hieromartyr Akepsimas of Persia commemorated on the same day.
11-3.desc: Venerable Akepsimas, hermit of Cyrrhus in Syria who lived enclosed in a cell for sixty years.
11-3.name: Akepsimas the Hermit

11-3.bio:
Saint Theodore was Bishop of Ancyra in Galatia. The synaxarion honours him as a confessor who suffered for the faith and reposed in peace.

No further details of his life are preserved.
11-3.desc: Saint Theodore the Confessor, Bishop of Ancyra.
11-3.name: Theodore of Ancyra

11-3.bio:
The holy martyrs Dasius, Severus, Andronas, Theodotus and Theodota are commemorated together. The synaxarion records that they suffered for Christ by the sword.

Nothing more is known of their lives.
11-3.desc: Holy Martyrs Dasius, Severus, Andronas, Theodotus and Theodota.
11-3.greek: Δάσιος, Σέβηρος, Άνδρωνας, Θεόδοτος και Θεοδότη
11-3.name: Dasius, Severus, Andronas, Theodotus and Theodota

11-3.bio:
Saint Achaemenides was the son of a distinguished Persian family in the early fifth century, during the reign of Yazdegerd. On becoming a Christian he abandoned his ancestral religion and possessions, and the king tried in vain to win him back.

Tradition relates that he was tortured and publicly humiliated, being set to tend the royal camels in rags, but persevered in the faith and confessed Christ to the end.
11-3.desc: Holy Confessor Achaemenides, a Persian nobleman who suffered for Christ under King Yazdegerd.
11-3.name: Achaemenides of Persia

11-30.bio:
St. Andrew, the First-Called of the Apostles, was a fisherman of Bethsaida and first a disciple of St. John the Forerunner. When the Baptist pointed to Jesus as the Lamb of God, Andrew followed Him at once and brought his brother Simon Peter to the Lord. After Pentecost, according to tradition, he preached the Gospel around the Black Sea and in Greece, and was martyred at Patras on a cross in the form of an X.

He is honored as patron of Greece and of the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople, whose first bishop tradition names him. His feast is kept on November 30.
11-30.desc: Holy First-Called Apostle Andrew, patron of Greece, Russia, and Scotland.
11-30.name: Andrew the First-Called

11-30.bio:
Saint Frumentius was a native of Tyre who, as a boy, was shipwrecked on the coast of Ethiopia with his brother Edesius and taken into the service of the king. Gaining influence at court, he encouraged the spread of Christianity in the country.

He later went to Alexandria, where Saint Athanasius consecrated him bishop for Ethiopia. He returned to baptize the king and people, and reposed in the fourth century.
11-30.desc: Saint Frumentius, Archbishop of Abyssinia, enlightener of Ethiopia.
11-30.name: Frumentius of Ethiopia

11-30.bio:
Saint Alexander was Bishop of Methymna on the island of Lesbos and is honoured in the synaxarion as a holy hierarch who reposed in peace.

No further details of his life are preserved.
11-30.desc: Saint Alexander, Bishop of Methymna on Lesbos.
11-30.name: Alexander of Methymna

11-4.bio:
Venerable Ioannikios the Great was born in Bithynia in the eighth century and served for years as a soldier before leaving the world for the monastic life on Mount Olympus in Asia Minor. There he lived in great asceticism and prayer, receiving gifts of prophecy and wonderworking, and he stood with the venerators of the holy icons in the troubled years of iconoclasm.

He reposed in peace in old age, revered by monks and hierarchs alike as one of the great ascetics of his time. He is commemorated on November 4.
11-4.name: Ioannikios the Great

11-4.bio:
Saints Nicander and Hermaeus lived in the first century and, according to tradition, were ordained by the Apostle Titus, Nicander as Bishop of Myra in Lycia and Hermaeus as a presbyter. They laboured to convert the pagans of the region.

Denounced to the governor Libanius, they were subjected to prolonged tortures and finally buried alive, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
11-4.desc: Hieromartyrs Nicander, Bishop of Myra, and Hermaeus the Presbyter, ordained by the Apostle Titus.
11-4.name: Nicander of Myra and Hermaeus

11-4.bio:
Saint Porphyrios was an actor at Ephesus in the fourth century. Tradition relates that while performing a parody of Christian Baptism on stage for the entertainment of the pagans, he was baptized in earnest and confessed Christ openly before the audience.

He was seized and beheaded for his confession.
11-4.desc: Holy Martyr Porphyrios the actor, who was converted while mocking Baptism on stage.
11-4.name: Porphyrios the Mime

11-4.bio:
Saint John Vatatzes was Emperor of Nicaea in the thirteenth century, ruling the Byzantine state in exile after the fall of Constantinople to the Crusaders. He was renowned for his justice, his generosity to the poor and his support of the Church and of learning.

He reposed in 1254 and was venerated as a saint soon after, especially at Magnesia where his relics were kept; he is honoured as John the Merciful, the Emperor.
11-4.desc: Saint John III Doukas Vatatzes, the merciful Emperor of Nicaea.
11-4.name: John Vatatzes the Merciful

11-4.bio:
Saint George Karslidis was born in Argyroupolis of Pontus at the beginning of the twentieth century and was ordained in Georgia, where he suffered imprisonment and persecution under the Soviet regime. He came to Greece as a refugee and founded the monastery of the Ascension at Sipsa near Drama.

Known for his ascetic life, discernment and spiritual counsel, he reposed in 1959 and was glorified by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 2008.
11-4.desc: Venerable George Karslidis the Confessor, elder of the Ascension monastery at Sipsa, Drama.
11-4.name: George Karslidis

11-4.bio:
Venerable Mercurius was a monk of the Kiev Caves Lavra who lived in the fourteenth century and is remembered for his strict fasting. His relics rest in the Far Caves of the Lavra.

He is commemorated in the Russian calendar both on this day and on November 24.
11-4.desc: Venerable Mercurius the Faster of the Kiev Caves Lavra.
11-4.name: Mercurius the Faster of the Kiev Caves

11-5.bio:
Saints Galaktion and Episteme were a young married couple of Emesa in Syria who, according to tradition, agreed to preserve chastity and gave themselves to the ascetic life, each entering a monastic community. When persecution arose, Galaktion was seized for his faith, and Episteme freely joined him in confessing Christ; together they endured torture and were put to death.

The Church honors them as a pair united first in marriage and finally in martyrdom. They are commemorated on November 5.
11-5.name: Galaktion and Episteme

11-5.bio:
The Apostles Hermas, Patrobas, Linus, Gaius and Philologus belonged to the Seventy and are mentioned by the Apostle Paul in his epistles. Tradition relates that Hermas became bishop of Philippopolis, Patrobas of Puteoli, Linus of Rome, Gaius of Ephesus and Philologus of Sinope.

Each laboured for the Gospel in his own see and reposed in peace.
11-5.desc: Holy Apostles of the Seventy Hermas, Patrobas, Linus, Gaius and Philologus, greeted by Saint Paul in his epistles.
11-5.greek: Ερμάς, Πατρόβας, Λίνος, Γάιος και Φιλόλογος
11-5.name: Hermas, Patrobas, Linus, Gaius and Philologus the Apostles

11-5.bio:
Saint Gregory was Archbishop of Alexandria in the ninth century. When the iconoclast emperor Leo the Armenian summoned him to Constantinople and demanded that he reject the holy icons, he confessed the Orthodox faith.

He was imprisoned and exiled, and reposed as a confessor after three years in prison.
11-5.desc: Saint Gregory the Confessor, Pope and Archbishop of Alexandria, who suffered under the iconoclasts.
11-5.name: Gregory of Alexandria

11-5.bio:
Saint Domninus suffered in Palestine during the persecution of Maximian, when Urban was governor of the province. After many tortures he was burned alive.

The synaxarion records that a number of Christian virgins were martyred together with him.
11-5.desc: Holy Martyr Domninus and the Christian virgins martyred with him in Palestine.
11-5.name: Domninus and companions

11-5.bio:
The holy martyrs Timothy, Theophilos and Theotimos suffered in Palestine under Maximian and the governor Urban. The synaxarion records that they were condemned to the beasts in the arena.

They are commemorated together with the martyr priest Dorotheos, who suffered in the same persecution.
11-5.desc: Holy Martyrs Timothy, Theophilos and Theotimos, who were given to wild beasts.
11-5.name: Timothy, Theophilos and Theotimos

11-5.bio:
The holy martyrs Eupsychios and Karterios suffered in Palestine under Maximian. The synaxarion records that they were mutilated and died confessing Christ.

No further details of their lives have been preserved.
11-5.desc: Holy Martyrs Eupsychios and Karterios, who suffered by mutilation for the faith.
11-5.name: Eupsychios and Karterios

11-5.bio:
Saint Jonah was Archbishop of Novgorod in the fifteenth century. Orphaned young, he was raised in piety and later became a monk and abbot before being chosen archbishop.

He was known for his care of the poor, his building of churches and monasteries, and his peacemaking between Novgorod and Moscow. He reposed in 1470.
11-5.desc: Saint Jonah the Wonderworker, Archbishop of Novgorod.
11-5.name: Jonah of Novgorod

11-6.bio:
St. Paul the Confessor was Archbishop of Constantinople in the fourth century, in the years when the Arian heresy was upheld by the powerful. A firm defender of the Nicene faith, he was driven from his see repeatedly by Arian opponents and finally exiled to a remote place, where he was put to death by those who hated his orthodoxy.

The Church honors him as a confessor who preferred exile and death to the betrayal of the true faith. He is commemorated on November 6.
11-6.name: Paul the Confessor

11-6.bio:
Saint Demetrianos was born in Cyprus in the ninth century. After the death of his young wife he became a monk, and later was consecrated Bishop of Kythrea, where he was known for his gentleness and works of mercy.

Tradition relates that when Arab raiders carried off many of his people, the aged bishop followed them to Baghdad and secured the captives' release. He reposed in peace and is greatly venerated in Cyprus.
11-6.desc: Saint Demetrianos, Bishop of Kythrea in Cyprus, wonderworker and protector of his flock.
11-6.name: Demetrianos of Kythrea

11-6.bio:
Venerable Barlaam was born in Novgorod in the twelfth century and, after the death of his parents, became a monk and settled at Khutyn on the Volkhov river, where he founded a monastery dedicated to the Transfiguration.

He was renowned for his ascetic life, his gift of prophecy and his miracles, and is among the most venerated saints of Novgorod.
11-6.desc: Venerable Barlaam, founder and abbot of the Khutyn monastery near Novgorod.
11-6.name: Barlaam of Khutyn

11-6.bio:
Venerable Luke was a monk of Sicily who lived in the ninth century. Tradition relates that he left the world as a young man, laboured in several monasteries and eventually became abbot, guiding many in the ascetic life.

He reposed in peace.
11-6.desc: Venerable Luke of Sicily, monk and abbot.
11-6.name: Luke of Sicily

11-6.bio:
Venerable Paul lived as a fool for Christ, hiding his ascetic life beneath apparent madness. Tradition places him at Corinth and relates that he bore mockery and abuse with patience while secretly practising prayer and fasting.

He reposed in peace.
11-6.desc: Venerable Paul the Fool-for-Christ of Corinth.
11-6.name: Paul the Fool-for-Christ

11-6.bio:
Venerable Luke was a monk of the Kiev Caves Lavra who served as steward of the monastery in the thirteenth century. His relics rest in the Far Caves.

He is remembered for his faithful stewardship and his life of humility.
11-6.desc: Venerable Luke, steward of the Kiev Caves Lavra.
11-6.name: Luke the Steward of the Kiev Caves

11-7.bio:
Venerable Lazaros of Mount Galesion was an ascetic of the eleventh century who, after years of pilgrimage and monastic labor in the Holy Land, settled on Mount Galesion near Ephesus. There he took up the harsh discipline of the stylites, living upon a pillar in prayer and fasting, and a community of monks gathered around him under his direction.

Renowned for discernment and compassion toward all who sought him out, he reposed in peace. He is commemorated on November 7.
11-7.name: Lazaros of Mount Galesion

11-7.bio:
Saint Hieron was a farmer of Tyana in Cappadocia who was conscripted into the army under Diocletian. When he and his companions refused to sacrifice to idols they were imprisoned at Melitene.

After tortures, Hieron and thirty-two others were beheaded. Tradition relates that his severed hand was later kept as a relic by his family.
11-7.desc: Holy Martyr Hieron and the thirty-two soldiers martyred with him at Melitene in Armenia.
11-7.greek: Άγιοι Τριάντα Τρεις Μάρτυρες εν Μελιτινή
11-7.name: Thirty-Three Martyrs of Melitene

11-7.bio:
Saints Melasippus and Kasine were a Christian couple of Ancyra who, with their young son Antoninus, were arrested under Julian the Apostate. The parents were tortured to death before the eyes of their son, who then confessed Christ himself and was beheaded.

Tradition relates that forty children who witnessed their courage believed in Christ and were martyred with them.
11-7.desc: Holy Martyrs Melasippus, his wife Kasine, their son Antoninus and forty children at Ancyra.
11-7.name: Melasippus, Kasine and Antoninus

11-7.bio:
Saint Thessalonica was a Christian woman of Amphipolis in Macedonia who, according to tradition, was driven from her home by her pagan father for her faith. Auctus and Taurion, moved by her confession, believed in Christ and were martyred.

Thessalonica herself endured her sufferings and reposed shortly afterwards. The three are commemorated together.
11-7.desc: Holy Martyrs Auctus, Taurion and Thessalonica, who suffered at Amphipolis in Macedonia.
11-7.name: Auctus, Taurion and Thessalonica

11-7.bio:
Saint Athenodoros is honoured as a martyr in the Church's calendar. Some sources identify him with the brother of Saint Gregory the Wonderworker, though this is uncertain.

No details of his martyrdom are preserved.
11-7.name: Athenodoros the Martyr

11-7.bio:
Saint Alexander was a Christian of Thessaloniki during the reign of Maximian. Tradition relates that when the emperor was offering sacrifice he overturned the altar, refusing to worship idols.

He was beheaded for his confession and is honoured as one of the martyrs of Thessaloniki.
11-7.desc: Holy Martyr Alexander of Thessaloniki, who suffered under Maximian.
11-7.name: Alexander of Thessaloniki

11-8.bio:
On November 8 the Church celebrates the Synaxis of the Archangels Michael and Gabriel together with all the Bodiless Powers of heaven. Michael, whose name asks Who is like God, is honored as the chief commander of the heavenly hosts who stood firm when the rebellious angels fell; Gabriel is the messenger who announced the Incarnation to the Theotokos.

The feast confesses the ministry of the angels, created spirits who glorify God and are sent for the aid of the faithful. It is one of the great name days of the Greek world, celebrated by those named Michael, Gabriel, and Angelos.
11-8.desc: Synaxis of the Chief Incorporeal Powers — Archangels Michael and Gabriel.
11-8.name: Synaxis of Archangels Michael and Gabriel

11-8.bio:
Saint Olga Michael was a Yup'ik woman of Kwethluk, Alaska, wife of the village priest and a midwife. She lived a hidden life of prayer, generosity to the poor and quiet care for women and children in her community, and reposed in 1979.

After her death many faithful reported her help, especially for those who had suffered abuse. She was glorified by the Orthodox Church in America in 2024 and is the first Yup'ik woman among the saints.
11-8.desc: Saint Olga of Kwethluk, Alaska, the Yup'ik midwife and matushka glorified in 2024.
11-8.name: Olga of Alaska

11-8.bio:
The monastery of the Archangel Michael Panormitis on Symi in the Dodecanese is one of the most famous places of pilgrimage in Greece. Its wonderworking icon of the Archangel draws pilgrims from across the islands and the seafaring communities.
